  already in front of the owner when it's given, never to anything requested or done *after* it. A

  multiple-choice answer is not an approval at all, even when an option's wording mentioned the
  action. (acting-approval-merge)

- **Calling `Edit` on a path outside the working directory and the session scratchpad** — a `Read`
  or a `Write` in this session is required first, and a shell write does not count; a narrow offset
  window satisfies it. Inside either root nothing is required, so read a file when you need to see
  it rather than to unlock it — Edit's tracking shows you nothing. (calling-edit-path)


- **Polling with an `until` loop** — write a condition that names the state awaited (a file's

  `# comment` on any line: interactive zsh treats `#` as a comment only under

# claudinite-growth — authoring Claudinite content here

- **Recording a local pack change** — automatic work writes no changelog file there: the commit
  and its PR are the record of *what* changed, and the *decision* (why, and why this carrier)
  is the entry on the element's provenance file, which the change carries. A local pack is
  neither versioned nor distributed, so a changelog file only aggregates unrelated changes into
  one line several runs a day contend for. A shared canon pack's version and its `VERSIONS.md`
  row are the canon's own tasks' to write, after the change lands - never the change's.
  (recording-local-pack)

- **Wanting a job to run in Actions** — make it a task with a `code_work` command rather than
  authoring a workflow; the vendored workflows already own the trigger, the concurrency, the
  secrets and the failure reporting. Work with no cadence is a task too, with no
  `preconditions`, woken by whatever knows the event happened. (wanting-job-run)

- **Writing a task here, or the skill one loads** — the corpus is `.claudinite/local/packs/` and
  no config widens it; a skill states the method and names no corpus, so the same action over a
  canon's `packs/` shelf is a `claudinite-canon-curation` task loading that same skill.
  (writing-task-skill)

- **Describing another pack's artifact** — point at the pack that owns it
  instead: the parenthetical costs this pack a version and a `VERSIONS.md` row every time that
  artifact changes, and the reader rarely needed it. (describing-another-packs)

- **A dispatched subagent's `completed` notification means its *turn* ended, not that its task did.** When its final text is a placeholder ("waiting for X to report back") rather than the report, read it as "stopped", resume the agent with a follow-up asking for the real output, and hand it any answer you already found rather than letting both sides re-derive it.

- **Before concluding a subagent whose handle went unreachable left no progress, check every channel it could have written to — not just git state and the dispatch's own PR comments.** A subagent that hits something worth escalating may have filed a tracker issue rather than a commit; a recovery check that reads only git and the dispatch thread reads "nothing survived" and relaunches a duplicate investigation that re-files the same finding.
  (concluding-subagent-handle)
- **Parallel background agents that each dump external content to disk need a collision-proof filename, not a shared generic one.** Subagents dispatched from one session share its scratchpad directory, so a fleet of them each told (or defaulting) to write the same generic path — a bare `log.jsonl`, `out.txt` — race on it: one agent's write can land mid-read by another, producing a truncated or mixed-content file with no error from either side. Give each agent's output a name that can't collide with its siblings' — the source item's own filename, or the agent's own session id — never a shared default.
  (parallel-background-agents)

Sort the items into a handful of groups whose members share what the verification has to read — the same area of the code, the same subsystem, the same one-line ask — and give each group to one child that returns one line per item.
  (choosing-fan-outs)
- **A fan-out spends the parent's own bound, so budget the wrap-up before dispatching.** The parent's clock runs while its children do, and the work the run exists to converge — the record it writes, the item it closes — has to fit inside that same bound. A parent that hands its whole budget to children returns too late to converge, leaving the item claimed until a janitor parks it as a failure the run never had; prefer a partial result inside the bound to a complete one outside it.
  (fan-out-spends)

## Updating an issue's status: comment, don't overwrite

To post a **status update** on an issue (the lifecycle's "update the issue's status" step, for a change that has one), use `add_issue_comment`. **Don't** reach for `issue_write` with `method: update` — that edits the issue itself and **replaces the whole body**, silently wiping the original description. ## 2026-09-14 · born · converted from references.md (git-github-advanced-1)
- **Reason:** GitHub's *Caching dependencies to speed up workflows* doc, "Restrictions for accessing
  a cache" and "Cache access for low-trust workflow triggers": a `pull_request` run's cache is
  created for `refs/pull/.../merge` and restorable only by re-runs of that PR; only `push`,
  `workflow_dispatch`, `repository_dispatch`, `delete`, `registry_package`, `page_build` and
  `schedule` may write the default branch's scope, every other trigger resolving there is read-only
  and a refused save "is reported as a warning in the workflow log"; entries "not accessed in over 7
  days" are removed. Read for #2012, where the read-only case is the executor's own `issues:
  labeled` trigger.
- **Mechanism:** a step of the git-github-advanced skill, a workflow

   (concluding-subagent-handle)
 - **Parallel background agents that each dump external content to disk need a collision-proof filename, not a shared generic one.** Subagents dispatched from one session share its scratchpad directory, so a fleet of them each told (or defaulting) to write the same generic path — a bare `log.jsonl`, `out.txt` — race on it: one agent's write can land mid-read by another, producing a truncated or mixed-content file with no error from either side. Give each agent's output a name that can't collide with its siblings' — the source item's own filename, or the agent's own session id — never a shared default.

+- **Prompting a subagent that needs a large or still-growing reference file's content — point it at the file's own path to read, rather than pasting the content into the prompt.** A paste is more expensive per dispatch than a read, and it carries a failure mode a path reference can't: a paste left as an unfilled template placeholder still dispatches without error, and the subagent runs on nothing.

 - **Choosing a fan-out's unit — group by what the children would share, never one child per item.** One subagent per work item is the tempting default and usually the wrong one: each child re-reads the same skill and re-derives the same view of the world to return a verdict that is most often "nothing to do", so the fan-out costs more than everything it decides. Sort the items into a handful of groups whose members share what the verification has to read — the same area of the code, the same subsystem, the same one-line ask — and give each group to one child that returns one line per item.
   (choosing-fan-outs)
 - **A fan-out spends the parent's own bound, so budget the wrap-up before dispatching.** The parent's clock runs while its children do, and the work the run exists to converge — the record it writes, the item it closes — has to fit inside that same bound. A parent that hands its whole budget to children returns too late to converge, leaving the item claimed until a janitor parks it as a failure the run never had; prefer a partial result inside the bound to a complete one outside it.

 ## Don't cite an issue or PR number before that object exists
 
-Issue and PR numbers share one counter per repo, so a comment or PR body written before its companion object is filed ("filed as a dedicated issue: #222") can end up citing the wrong number once that object actually lands and consumes a different one. ## 2026-09-14 · born · converted from references.md (git-github-advanced-1)
- **Reason:** GitHub's *Caching dependencies to speed up workflows* doc, "Restrictions for accessing
  a cache" and "Cache access for low-trust workflow triggers": a `pull_request` run's cache is
  created for `refs/pull/.../merge` and restorable only by re-runs of that PR; only `push`,
  `workflow_dispatch`, `repository_dispatch`, `delete`, `registry_package`, `page_build` and
  `schedule` may write the default branch's scope, every other trigger resolving there is read-only
  and a refused save "is reported as a warning in the workflow log"; entries "not accessed in over 7
  days" are removed. Read for #2012, where the read-only case is the executor's own `issues:
  labeled` trigger.

input.title: Promote 8 lessons from member local packs (chrome-extension, node, html, basics, claudinite-growth, claude-code-web-users-support, git-github)
input.body:
Growth-promote run over the members named in #2269's Context: ClaudiniteCanary, ClaudiniteWebsite, CrosswordChat, EdFringeNow, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, MissingBulbWebsite, NoRFinder, Shepherd, TLDR, VascularColoring.

## Promoted (8)

- **`chrome-extension`** — a `declarativeContent`/`UrlFilter` host match can't be verified by CDP introspection or a jsdom-style harness; only a real-Chrome, loaded-extension test exercises it. From GoogleCalendarEventCreator's `declarativecontent-urlfilter-host`.
- **`node`** — the jsdom-vs-Chrome `<noscript>`/`<script>`/`<style>` divergence is a production bug (a scraper, any DOM-emulation library reading foreign HTML), not only a testing gotcha; strip those tags before reading `textContent`. From GoogleCalendarEventCreator's `jsdom-chrome-dom`.
- **`html`** — diagnosing a "the live page shows wrong data" report starts with the browser's own evidence (Network tab, Application/Storage), before building a speculative local repro, which can converge on a plausible-but-wrong root cause that reproduces the identical symptom. From EdFringeNow's "Get the browser's own evidence before guessing a repro for a live-data bug report".
- **`basics`** (4) — auditing each occurrence's actual referent before applying a bulk terminology rename an owner approved only in free text (ClaudiniteWebsite); offering restructuring itself as an `AskUserQuestion` option for a structural complaint, not just mechanism-level tweaks (EdFringeNow); computing a duration written into a commit/PR from real timestamps, never a felt sense of elapsed time around an unconsumed background wait (EdFringeNow); dropping straight to the plain unsubstituted form of a Bash command naming `git` that a worktree-isolated agent refuses as "too complex to verify" when compounded (EdFringeNow).
- **`claudinite-growth`** (2) — never landing a lesson that teaches a future session to retry, ignore or explain away a permission/security/classifier denial, however much retry evidence backs it (EdFringeNow); pointing a subagent at a large or growing reference file's own path to read, rather than pasting the content into the prompt — cheaper, and immune to an unfilled-placeholder paste (Shepherd, folded into the `unattended-agents` skill).
- **`claude-code-web-users-support`** — a scratch clone of a repo outside this session's own GitHub scope fetches fine but pushes `403`; finish and verify the change there, then hand it off as a patch for a session whose scope reaches that repo. Generalized from ClaudiniteWebsite's `fix-belongs-canon`/`writing-skill-fix`.

## Sharpened (1)

- **`git-github` (`git-github-advanced` skill)** — corrected "comments generally have no reliable edit path to fix a wrong citation": `update_issue_comment` does fix one already posted (works on a PR's conversation comments too). From MissingBulbWebsite's `citing-unfiled-issue`.

## Also fixed

Three provenance files this PR's first commit landed as a bare one-line sentence with no entry heading, which fails this canon's own provenance grammar (`text outside an entry`, caught by `provenance.mjs check`): `chrome-extension/provenance/declarativecontent-real-chrome-only.md`, `node/provenance/jsdom-divergence-hits-production.md`, `html/provenance/gather-evidence-before-repro.md`. Each now carries its source member's full (reduced) history plus the promoted entry.

Each landed item is generalized (project specifics stripped from the rule text; the provenance file keeps the incident) and deduped against the whole corpus before landing.

## Notable rejections (not promoted — already covered)

Several members independently rediscovered the same GitHub-MCP-tool-result-size lesson (narrow `fields`/`perPage`, read the spilled `{total_count, items}` envelope on overflow) — GoogleCalendarEventCreator, TLDR, MissingBulbWebsite, Shepherd, EdFringeNow, WIP. All of it is already covered, in more depth, by `packs/git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md` and `packs/basics/declared-checks.json`'s `github-list-without-fields` check — nothing landed from this cluster.

Also rejected as already covered: MissingBulbWebsite's `merge_pull_request`-after-force-push-500 and add-a-commit-don't-force-push rules, TLDR's `list_pull_requests` `merged`-field gotcha, Shepherd's PR-diff-view-drops-a-new-file and shared-scratchpad-filename-collision rules (all already in `git-github-advanced` or `unattended-agents`); GoogleCalendarEventCreator's `get_job_logs`/`tail_lines` overflow (already in `git-github-advanced`, down to the same measured `tail_lines: 2406`); VascularColoring's and NoRFinder's research-project restatements (already in the adopted `research-project` pack, several verbatim); Shepherd's "retiring a system" and "reading the mount vs canon main" rules (already basics/claudinite-lifecycle canon, verbatim); GoogleCalendarEventCreator's chrome-extension/node/html duplicates of what this same PR already promotes.

Refs #2269, #2304

entries.name: mcp__github__add_issue_comment
entries.description: Add a comment and/or reaction to a specific issue or issue comment in a GitHub repository. Use this tool with pull requests as well (in this case pass pull request number as issue_number), but only if user is not asking specifically to add or react to review comments. At least one of body or reaction is required.

body.description: Comment content. Required unless reaction is provided.

comment_id.description: The numeric ID of the issue or pull request comment to react to. Use this for reactions to comments; omit it to react to the issue or pull request itself. Cannot be combined with body.

issue_number.description: Issue or pull request number to comment on or react to.

reaction.description: Emoji reaction to add. Required unless body is provided.

entries.name: mcp__github__issue_write
entries.description: Create a new or update an existing issue in a GitHub repository.

assignees.description: Usernames to assign to this issue

duplicate_of.description: Issue number that this issue is a duplicate of. Required when state_reason is 'duplicate'.

delete.description: Set to true to clear this field's current value on the issue. When false or omitted, this property is ignored. Cannot be true when 'value' or 'field_option_name' is provided.

field_name.description: Issue field name (case-insensitive). Must match a field returned by list_issue_fields for this repository or its organization.

field_option_name.description: Option name for single-select fields. Validated against the field's options before the API call. Cannot be combined with 'value' or 'delete: true'.

value.description: Value to set. Use for text, number, and date fields (date as YYYY-MM-DD). For single-select fields, prefer 'field_option_name' so the option is validated before the API call. Cannot be combined with 'field_option_name' or 'delete: true'.

issue_fields.description: Issue field values to set or clear. Each item requires 'field_name' and exactly one of 'value', 'field_option_name', or 'delete: true'.

labels.description: Labels to apply to this issue

method.description:
Write operation to perform on a single issue.
Options are:
- 'create' - creates a new issue.
- 'update' - updates an existing issue.

parent_issue_number.description: Issue number of the parent issue. Only used when method is 'create' and cannot be combined with issue_fields. The new issue is created and attached to this parent in the same operation.

parent_owner.description: Repository owner of the parent issue. Must be provided with parent_repo. Omit both to use owner and repo. Only used when method is 'create' and parent_issue_number is provided.

parent_repo.description: Repository name of the parent issue. Must be provided with parent_owner. Omit both to use owner and repo. Only used when method is 'create' and parent_issue_number is provided.

state_reason.description: Reason for the state change. Ignored unless state is changed.

type.description: Type of this issue. For updates, pass null to remove the current type. Only use if issue types are enabled for this repository. Use list_issue_types to get valid type values for this repository or its owner organization. If the repository doesn't support issue types, omit this parameter.
